tool.name: KuwaharaFilter
tool.summary: Kuwahara filter: an edge-preserving smoother. The window is split into four overlapping quadrants that share the centre cell, and the cell takes the mean of the quadrant with the least variance, so domains are flattened while their edges stay sharp.
tool.usage:
No-data cells are left out of each quadrant.

With a large window the classic filter breaks the grid into square patches (the four quadrants are squares, and each cell takes only one of them): tick Generalized Kuwahara to avoid them.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: window_size
param.dialogReference: Width of the window in pixels (odd); the quadrants are (size + 1) / 2 pixels across.
param.pythonReference: Width of the window in pixels (odd); the quadrants are (size + 1) / 2 pixels across.

param.name: generalized
param.dialogReference: Generalized Kuwahara filter (Papari, Petkov & Campisi 2007): the circular window (radius = half the window size) is Gaussian-weighted and divided into 8 overlapping sectors, and the cell takes the mean of the sector means weighted by their standard deviation to the power -8. Steps stay sharp, without the classic filter's square patches; slower.
param.pythonReference: Generalized Kuwahara filter (Papari, Petkov & Campisi 2007): the circular window (radius = half the window size) is Gaussian-weighted and divided into 8 overlapping sectors, and the cell takes the mean of the sector means weighted by their standard deviation to the power -8. Steps stay sharp, without the classic filter's square patches; slower.
